relay:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make a wide polished 1536x1024 GAMEPLAY DESIGN STUDY board, not a screenshot of implemented software. Reference image is the approved Relay Raiders board. Use ONLY its LEFT gameplay as the locked visual style: exact crescent graphite/violet carrier, huge segmented violet iris, chrome blue cannons, glazed cyan/violet/X bricks, very dark blue space background. Ignore all right-hand characters and fish; NO characters, pilots, fish, crew faces or portrait buttons in this new board. Keep the existing ship silhouette and level proportions recognizably exact. Glossy Blender Cycles vinyl/ceramic/chrome, warm upper-left key, soft blue rim, pink bounce, saturated but not neon, minimal yellow. Dark calm near-black planets never overpower the foreground.
Composition: four equally sized tall portrait PLAYFIELD panels in one row on a navy editorial board. Full-screen game fields, no phone hardware. Preserve generous lower reaction space and the low wide cyan/chrome paddle. Put clean short labels OUTSIDE panels. Main heading exactly "LEVEL 2 — RELAY RAIDERS". First two panels grouped under "A — CIRCUIT BREAKOUT"; last two under "B — ESCORT RUN". Footer exactly "DESIGN STUDY — NEW MECHANICS AND ASSETS NOT YET BUILT".
Panel1 caption "LINK THE CIRCUIT": four original tall station housings now contain glossy mechanical relay coils, never faces. One housing lit cyan, two already linked by a subtle segmented circuit path. Original 30-brick banks stay source-faithful. Chrome ordinary ball visibly banking from the low paddle toward active relay. No crew rescue or kidnapping.
Panel2 caption "EARN THE SHIP BURST": same environment. After two links, the lower paddle has transformed into a small EMPTY silver/cyan combat skiff derived from the reference B skiff, now pointing UPFIELD with registered short blue thrusters beneath. No duplicate upper parked skiff. Two thin bright laser bolts leave visible dorsal emitters toward the now-open iris; a chrome ball sits safely in its nose cradle. This is a joyful short firing phase with readable space, not a screen-filling beam. Source-faithful industrial styling, no cartoon stickers.
Panel3 caption "CLEAR THE CARGO ROUTE": same source B carrier and brick banks, lower paddle still present. One EMPTY silver/cyan cargo skiff sits midway along the central lane, a translucent dotted route connects two compact checkpoint pads to the iris. Some central breakable modules obstruct the route; ordinary ball is about to break one. Housings are now sealed empty industrial buffer machinery. No crew. Only one skiff exists. One small warned cannon/core lane is legible, not a beam through solid cover.
Panel4 caption "ESCORT THROUGH THE GATE": same cargo skiff now reaches the open iris above, checkpoint pads show small green completion marks, central blocker bricks are cleared, a restrained outward relief ripple and a few glossy shards communicate payoff. Paddle and ordinary ball remain playable below. No new portraits or companion anatomy.
Only compact pause/lives/score at top in-game, no panels of instructions, no repeated aim/drag/catch text. Match the supplied art quality exactly. All novel machinery must look like real independent glossy rendered objects with thickness, mounts, material and highlights, not flat vector placeholders.
orbital:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make a wide polished 1536x1024 GAMEPLAY DESIGN STUDY board for LEVEL3, using the reference Orbital Breakout image. LOCK the exact LEFT playfield visual family: angular slate/violet mothership with round magenta command optic, central shuttered bay and opaque lower lip, large pink/cyan cannons, source-like glazed cyan/violet/X bricks, low wide chrome/cyan paddle and chrome balls. Ignore ALL right-hand Nova/Pin/character artwork. No crew, robot faces, pilots or portraits in this board. Calm near-black Saturn/star field, dim planet behind foreground. Glossy Blender Cycles look, warm upper-left key, cool rim, pink bounce, clear ceramic highlights, saturated not neon, minimal yellow.
Four equal tall portrait playfields across one wide navy board. Short clean labels OUTSIDE panels. Main heading exactly "LEVEL 3 — ORBITAL BREAKOUT". First two grouped "A — SHUTTER FORGE", last two grouped "B — ORBITAL SWITCH". Footer exactly "DESIGN STUDY — NEW MACHINERY AND GAMEPLAY NOT YET BUILT".
Panel1 caption "TIME THE OPENING": replace all three tall crew housings with visibly EMPTY industrial stabiliser machines in the same triangle positions. Thick graphite frame, glossy energy coil, folding mechanical leaf and visible hinge. Left machine has a genuinely open leaf and exposed cyan coil, right and low centre shut. One ordinary chrome ball approaches the open coil from the low paddle. Subtle local arc shows remaining opening, no global rescue clock. Closed pieces are visibly solid. Preserve the rest of source brick banks.
Panel2 caption "EARN THE COLLAPSE": stabilisers visibly disabled, two side support banks crumble in a controlled stagger, a few chunky ceramic pieces clear outward above the reaction lane. Exactly THREE ordinary chrome balls release into the open middle. A solid projection ARM unfolds in FRONT of the intact mothership lip and presents a tangible glowing reactor outside and BELOW the ship at roughly world(180,246), with a broad clear ordinary-ball approach. Never depict a ball phasing through the opaque lower lip or an inaccessible interior target. Cannons quiet; this is a satisfying hazard-free release and readable finishing target.
Panel3 caption "BEND THE BALL": same C ship but former housings are new empty magnetic projectors. Left low-opacity cyan curl field and right violet curl field with visible small solid bases, lower centre is neutraliser. A rising chrome ball takes a short bounded cyan-curved path toward the matching segment of a three-petal receiver ring EXTERNALLY projected below the lip at world(180,255). Returning balls and paddle lane remain straight. No laser or pilot ship phase. Arcs are restrained and don't obscure the real bricks.
Panel4 caption "OVERLOAD THE RING": all three receiver tags solved; three physical petals fold OUTWARD to reveal an external central core with a broad visible opening. Fields and guns off. One straight chrome ball is near the exposed core, several glossy panel chunks lift outward in a calm victorious cascade. Paddle stays at the bottom. No repeated crew rescue and no long beams.
The new machinery and projectors must be detailed volumetric glossy rendered game assets with readable pivot/hinge/coil shapes, not hand-drawn diagrams or cheap flat overlays. Keep the exact approved mothership silhouette and source quality. Only compact top pause/lives/score, no verbose instructions or bottom panels. No artwork of characters anywhere.
